I've been farming this land in Quzhou for 50 years, and I know every piece of it. Last year my wheat averaged about 480 jin per mu and the maize did about 520 jin. This year I'm not changing much — at 73 years old, I stick with what I know works.

For the winter wheat, I plant an improved variety, the kind the seed dealer in town has been selling for a few years now. My neighbor Lao Zhang uses it and gets good stands. I rotary till the field in early October before sowing, break up the soil fine. For fertilizer, I put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — that gives me roughly 15 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium. Then when the wheat greens up and hits jointing in March, I topdress another 20 kg of urea per mu, which is about 9 kg more nitrogen. The extension fellow once told me 20 kg nitrogen total is enough, but I've always done a bit more. I'd rather waste some fertilizer than risk a thin crop — a bad wheat harvest is a disaster for my family. I irrigate three times: wintering water before the freeze, jointing water in spring, and one at grain filling. The pump electricity costs me, but three waters is what this wheat needs. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once after the wheat turns green, and I spray fungicide and insecticide together once if I see rust or aphids coming.

For the summer maize, the window is tight — only a few days after wheat harvest in June. I don't have time to plough deep, so I do no-tillage planting, just sow the hybrid maize seed right into the wheat stubble with the planter. I put compound fertilizer down at planting, about 40 kg per mu — that's around 12 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium. At the big trumpet stage I topdress with 15 kg urea per mu, about another 7 kg nitrogen. Total nitrogen around 19-20 kg. I irrigate twice: once if the seedlings look dry after planting, and once at tasseling — that tasseling water is the most important, you can't skip it. I spray herbicide right after planting, and if the corn borer shows up I spray insecticide once in mid-July.

My whole farm is 16.9 mu, all in wheat-maize rotation. My son and daughter-in-law work in the factory in Handan and send money back, so I can afford the inputs. But fertilizer prices keep going up, and every yuan matters. Still, I won't cut back — losing yield hurts far more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer.
